title: Zenith GPU Systems - Redwood Partner Intro
summary: Introductory discovery between Redwood (AE+SE) and Zenith GPU Systems to explore a channel/reseller partnership and technical integration for dedicated GPU capacity. Covered partner program basics, integration patterns (private/private control plane, marketplace, API forwarding), typical enterprise concerns (SAML, SOC2, KMS), and go-to-market alignment. Agreed next steps: share partner deck, run a quick benchmark with H100 nodes, follow up on contractual/commerce flow details.
next_steps: Lena - send partner deck, reseller pricing grid, and security one-pager by 2026-06-04
Jordan - propose benchmark plan (3 models, latency/cost targets) and sample workload by 2026-06-08
Raj - share Zenith's typical procurement timeline and list of target accounts by 2026-06-07
Schedule technical follow-up (deep dive on private deployment) week of 2026-06-15
action_items: Lena Park - Email partner deck + pricing + marketing co-sell assets - due 2026-06-04
Jordan Kim - Draft benchmark test plan (H100 + A100, 8/16GB, perf/cost) - due 2026-06-08

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-01 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Jordan Kim (Redwood SE), Raj Patel (Zenith), Maya Chen (Zenith), Diego Alvarez (Zenith)

[00:00] Lena Park: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. I'm Lena from Redwood, AE on the partnerships team. With me is Jordan, our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:09] Raj Patel: Doing well, thanks. Excited to chat, we had a quick sync internally and want to explore how Zenith and Redwood might partner - both from a channel and a tech integration point.
[00:18] Jordan Kim: Awesome. Quick agenda - high level partner program, technical integration patterns (hosted api vs dedicated vs private), security/compliance checklist, and then next steps. Fine?
[00:27] Maya Chen: Sounds good. We'll do intro too: I'm Maya, tech partnerships. Diego will cover infra details.
[00:32] Diego Alvarez: Hey all.
[00:34] [00:45] Lena Park: Great. Raj, can you give a bit of context on Zenith's go-to-market and the kinds of customers you think would want dedicated GPU capacity vs managed endpoints?
[00:52] Raj Patel: Sure. Zenith sells GPU clouds to ISVs and telco customers, lots of infra and channel deals. We're seeing interest in packaged inference for enterprise customers - low latency w/ single-tenant, and also a lot of startups that want cost-effective burst capacity. We're thinking a partnership where we can resell Redwood's Dedicated offering or integrate our provisioning to route traffic into Redwood private deployments.
[01:12] Jordan Kim: Got it. When you say private deployments, do you mean VPC peering or an on-prem option?
[01:18] Diego Alvarez: We support both. We have customers with strict data residency and air-gap requirements. Budget and procurement vary.
[01:24] [01:30] Jordan Kim: Cool. To set expectations: Redwood has three main modes - Hosted API for fast time-to-value, Dedicated reserved pools for predictable throughput, and Private (customer-controlled control plane, VPC/on-prem) for regulated workloads. The same API surface across those modes, which helps for channel partners.
[01:46] Maya Chen: We like that. A couple quick questions on security: SOC 2, SAML/SSO, KMS compatibility - are those table stakes today?
[01:55] Lena Park: Absolutely. We support SOC 2, SAML/SSO integrations and customer-managed KMS/HSM for Private. We also produce audit logs per request and token-level cost/latency breakdown in the Console.
[02:08] Raj Patel: Nice. For resale we need clear partner pricing and margin, and flow for procurement - is there a marketplace approach or would it be direct billing?
[02:18] Lena Park: Both are possible. We have reseller/partner tiers: referral, reseller with billing pass-through, and a white-label co-sell model. We can share the partner deck that outlines margin bands.
[02:30] [02:45] Diego Alvarez: From a technical perspective, we want to understand supported GPU SKUs - H100, A100, etc - and quantization/throughput tradeoffs. For some customers, 8-bit quantized models are fine; others need FP16. Any kernel/compilation constraints?
[02:58] Jordan Kim: Great question. Our runtime supports a range of hardware profiles. We optimize kernels and can recommend quantization profiles per model. For H100 we can drive very high throughput; A100 is common too. We also handle batching and KV cache to reduce cost. Note transcription: sometimes our internal docs call it "K-V cache" or "KV cache" - occasionally transcribed differently.
[03:20] Raj Patel: Cool. For channel deals we'd like the ability to run a benchmark that simulates our customer workloads - end-to-end latency plus token cost.
[03:28] Jordan Kim: That makes sense. We usually recommend a 3-model benchmark: a smaller completion model, a chat style LLM, and an embedding workload. We can run the tests on H100 and A100 configs and provide latency p50/p90, throughput, and per-token cost.
[03:42] Maya Chen: And can you support region-specific deployments? Our EU customers have data residency needs.
[03:48] Lena Park: Yes, we have hosted regions in NA and EU and Private can be deployed into the customer's VPC or on-prem. We can also do contractual data residency terms.
[03:58] [04:15] Raj Patel: On the go-to-market side, we'd want co-marketing, joint webinars, and a technical enablement pack. Is there an enablement kit?
[04:24] Lena Park: Yes, we provide docs, sample code, joint case study templates, and a partner portal. We'll include marketing co-sell assets in the deck.
[04:33] Diego Alvarez: For the technical integration, what's the simplest approach - API forwarding or a managed connector?
[04:39] Jordan Kim: Simplest is API forwarding: Zenith proxies customer requests to Redwood's Hosted or Dedicated endpoints with your credentials. For deeper integrations, customers can choose Dedicated and we can integrate provisioning APIs so Zenitih's control plane can spin up Redwood capacity programmatically. Private deployments require a bit more work (networking, KMS), but give full isolation.
[04:59] Raj Patel: Are there limits on model catalog? Can we offer third-party models or only Redwood-curated ones?
[05:06] Jordan Kim: We have a model catalog of curated open models and Redwood-verified performance profiles. There's flexibility for customers to bring their own models for Private deployments; for Hosted we curate and manage the variants.
[05:17] [05:30] Maya Chen: Procurement/contract Q: our customers often require specific SOC/ISO language, SLA commitments and security addendum. Do you have an enterprise contract template?
[05:39] Lena Park: Yes, we have enterprise SLAs for Dedicated and Private, plus security addendums. We'll share those docs under NDA - typical stuff like uptime targets, response times, and data handling.
[05:47] Raj Patel: Speaking of SLA, what's typical latency we can promise?
[05:52] Jordan Kim: Latency depends heavily on model size, sequence length, and batching strategy. For chat style models on Dedicated H100 we typically see single-digit 100ms-300ms p50 for small-to-medium models; larger context or larger models will push that up. We can share performance profiles.
[06:09] Diego Alvarez: And pricing? Ballpark per-token or per-hour for reserved capacity?
[06:14] Lena Park: We have usage-based pricing for Hosted (per-token/per-embedding), and reserved capacity contracts for Dedicated (monthly/annual commit). Exact numbers depend on SKU (H100 vs A100), utilization, and support tier. We'll send a pricing grid.
[06:26] [06:45] Raj Patel: Competitors: some of our customers already run on Lambda or CoreWeave - how is Redwood different?
[06:53] Jordan Kim: The differentiation is a production-first developer experience with unified serving across hosted/dedicated/private, plus cost-aware performance controls (batching, caching, quantization) and built-in rollouts/traceability. We aim to reduce the operational burden of serving LLMs at scale.
[07:06] Maya Chen: Good. For a pilot, what would you recommend?
[07:10] Jordan Kim: A short pilot: run benchmarks on a representative workload, then do a proof of concept with 1-2 anchor customers using Dedicated or Private depending on requirements. For reseller flows we can pilot referral deals and measure conversion.
[07:21] Raj Patel: Sounds reasonable. From Zenith's side, we can provide a testbed account and a list of target customers for early outreach.
[07:28] [07:45] Diego Alvarez: A couple of nitty-gritty: network egress costs if you route through REDWOOD hosted endpoints - can you estimate that?
[07:52] Lena Park: Egress depends on the cloud region/provider. For Dedicated/Private deployments inside the customer's VPC, egress is typically internal. For Hosted we can provide estimates but you'll want to consider bandwidth patterns. We'll include example cost worksheets.
[08:06] Maya Chen: Also: SSO integration - do you support Okta/SAML?
[08:11] Lena Park: Yes, Okta SAML is supported; we also support SCIM for provisioning.
[08:17] [08:30] Raj Patel: On the legal side: revenue share, billing flow, and distributor agreement - we need a template.
[08:36] Lena Park: We'll share the partner agreement templates; finance ops can loop in later.
[08:40] Jordan Kim: Quick note: some customers care deeply about determinism on model outputs for regulatory reasons; we have version pinning and reproducible configs to help there.
[08:52] Raj Patel: Good to know.
[08:55] [09:15] Maya Chen: Any references or case studies of similar channel partners?
[09:20] Lena Park: We have a few: a cloud partner that resells Dedicated capacity and an SI that integrates our Private deployments for a financial customer. We'll include anonymized case studies in the deck.
[09:32] Diego Alvarez: One technical ask: can Redwood expose a webhook or event stream with request-level audit logs to our SIEM?
[09:40] Jordan Kim: Yes, audit logs can be exported; we support syslog/S3 export and webhooks - some customers push logs into Splunk/other SIEMs.
[09:48] [10:10] Raj Patel: For the benchmark, what's a realistic timeline? Two weeks to get results?
[10:15] Jordan Kim: If you can provide the sample workloads and account access, we can run an initial benchmark in ~1 week, then iterate.
[10:21] Lena Park: We'll scope it as: Jordan drafts test plan, Zenith provides workload and target SKUs, Redwood runs on shared capacity or Dedicated trial, then we share results.
[10:33] [10:45] Maya Chen: A couple risks: some customers won't allow external managed keys - they'd need HSM/KMS in their VPC. How does Redwood handle BYOK?
[10:56] Jordan Kim: For Private we can support customer-managed KMS/HSM. Hosted can integrate with customer KMS with additional controls but often customers want Private for strict BYOK.
[11:10] Raj Patel: Noted. Anything else on integration?
[11:12] Lena Park: We discussed model catalog, network, benchmark, security, pricing, and GTM. Next steps captured.
[11:19] [11:30] Raj Patel: Quick comment: channel enablement - can we get a technical enablement call for our sales engineers next week?
[11:37] Lena Park: Yes, we can do a deep-dive SE enablement. I'll coordinate.
[11:41] Jordan Kim: We'll include an optional deep dive on Private deployment networking and KMS.
[11:47] Maya Chen: Great.
[11:49] [12:00] Diego Alvarez: Final question - are there any hard blockers for an initial pilot from Redwood's side?
[12:06] Jordan Kim: No major blockers. We just need the workload specs and to agree on SKUs and scope. If it's Private, we'll need network access and a bit more lead time.
[12:18] Raj Patel: OK. Let's talk timelines - procurement cycles for our enterprise customers are often 6-12 weeks. For pilot customers we can move faster.
[12:28] Lena Park: Understood. We'll tailor the pilot to short timelines where possible.
[12:33] [12:45] Summary/Recap:
- Redwood to send partner deck, pricing grid, security one-pager.
- Jordan to propose benchmark plan for H100/A100.
- Zenith to share list of target accounts and procurement windows.
- Schedule SE enablement + technical deep dive week of 2026-06-15.

[13:10] Action items reiterated: see meeting notes.
[13:15] Raj Patel: Thanks everyone - this was super helpful. Looking forward to the deck.
[13:20] Lena Park: Thanks all. We'll follow up with the materials and a calendar invite for the deep dive.
[13:25] Meeting ended.

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hearings present (e.g., "K-V cache" vs "KV cache", Redwood product names sometimes spoken quickly). Some proper nouns may be incorrect in automated transcript and should be validated before legal or procurement attachments.
